name: 7-epbs
title: EPBS — End-product breakdown
subtitle: One configuration item per thing procured, built or delivered, each with its contract as a requirement definition and a verification case that checks it.

setup.js: (() => { const api = window.sysml; const p = api.byName('SurveillanceDroneSwarm::EPBS::batteryPacks').id; const c = api.byName('SurveillanceDroneSwarm::EPBS::BatteryPackContract').id; const hits = api.descendants(api.byName('SurveillanceDroneSwarm::EPBS').id).filter((e) => e.eClass === 'Satisfy' && e.source?.[0] === p && e.target?.[0] === c); if (hits.length !== 1) throw new Error('satisfy BatteryPackContract by batteryPacks: found ' + hits.length); api.delete(hits[0].id); })()

steps.label: SHOW ONLY THE EPBS LAYER
steps.text: In the Explorer, ⊞ on EPBS scopes every diagram to the end-product breakdown: one configuration item per thing procured, built or delivered.

steps.label: GENERAL VIEW
steps.text: Sixteen configuration items, each drawn with its fielded usage, its contract and its verification case. Too small to read whole, so pick one.

steps.label: READ ONE ITEM
steps.text: Select BatteryPack, press Selection. Around it: its contract, its verification case and a hazard. Properties lists its «Trace» with SwarmMember, the PA part it realises.

steps.label: INTERCONNECTION VIEW
steps.text: No wiring at this level: 16 item definitions and their 16 fielded usages. Counts sit on the usages: select batteryPacks, Multiplicity 24.

steps.label: REQUIREMENT VIEW
steps.text: Each fielded usage satisfies its item's contract, as storeForwardSoftware does ReportStoreForwardSoftwareContract. Before recording we deleted one of these links.

steps.label: A CONTRACT ON ITS OWN
steps.text: BatteryPackContract is now satisfied by nothing. Its text: at least 40 minutes of flight, a swap in no more than 20 minutes, at least two qualified sources.

steps.label: DRAW A SATISFY LINK
steps.text: Pick Satisfy in the palette, then click the fielded usage first: batteryPacks, which now satisfies only the battery-supplier hazard.

steps.label: THEN CLICK THE CONTRACT
steps.text: Then click the contract it satisfies, BatteryPackContract. The link is created and selected, and the diagram is laid out again.

steps.label: THE RESULT
steps.text: batteryPacks satisfies BatteryPackContract again. The file gets the same line back, satisfy BatteryPackContract by batteryPacks, at the end of EPBS.

steps.label: PARAMETRIC VIEW
steps.text: 48 constraints: each contract's assume and require, with its condition written in the box, and each verification's objective, which only names the contract it verifies.

steps.label: READ ONE CONTRACT'S CONDITIONS
steps.text: Zoomed in, the first pair: DroneAirframeContract assumes a full charge at the start, and requires at least 40 minutes of flight and 18 m/s cruise.

steps.label: CASE VIEW
steps.text: The verification cases, one per contract. Each is drawn with its subject, the item under test, and its objective, which in the text names the contract it verifies.

steps.label: READ ONE CASE
steps.text: VerifyBatteryPack: a discharge test for endurance, a timed swap at the recharge point and an audit of sources. Its subject, pack, is the item under test.

steps.label: TREE VIEW
steps.text: What EPBS contains, one branch at a time. Select BatteryPackContract: +4 on its box opens its subject pack, its id and its two constraints, assume and require.

outro.title: Explore it, then propose a change
outro.text: The live model: cosmindxu.github.io/mbse-workflow. Edits come back through GitHub: see CONTRIBUTING.md, “Proposing a change to the model”.
